data.paper_title: The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns
data.selected_experiment: Table VI, Panel B: value-weighted quintile portfolios sorted on idiosyncratic volatility relative to the Fama-French (1993) three-factor model (1/0/1 strategy)

economic_rationale.value: The paper tests whether stocks with high idiosyncratic volatility relative to FF-3 have high exposure to aggregate volatility risk, which carries a negative price of risk; it finds this explains very little of the low returns and calls the pattern a puzzle. The result runs opposite to theories (e.g. Merton 1987) predicting a positive idiosyncratic volatility premium.

unresolved_details: Stock universe and filters for the idiosyncratic volatility sorts are not stated (exchanges, share codes, price filters); the minimum of more than 17 daily observations is stated only for the beta-to-delta-VIX regressions.
Whether equation (8) uses excess or raw daily stock returns is not stated.
Breakpoint universe is not named explicitly; equal-count quintiles over all stocks is implied by quintile 5 containing 20% of the stocks.
Date of the market capitalization used for value weights is not stated.

Exact window end for 'the past month' (calendar month ending at formation date) and the timing of the 1/0/1 formation are not spelled out; the paper adds a 1/1/1 variant to ensure information is definitely available at time t.
Treatment of delisting returns and the return convention for holding-period returns beyond 'total, not excess, simple returns' are not stated.
Source of the daily Fama-French factors is not stated.
The paper has two central experiments (Table I, beta-to-delta-VIX sorts; Table VI, idiosyncratic volatility sorts); Table VI Panel B was selected as the headline low-volatility result.
